issues.body: sanitize_message removes only `\n` before calling sanitize_subject. For a line such as `claim 0123abcd [redacted-account] bench/impl\r\n`, the subject passed to LEGACY_CLAIM_SUBJECT_RE ends in `\r`, so the `$`-anchored pattern does not match and the handle remains. In contrast, scan uses message.splitlines(), which strips the CRLF and classifies the same line as a legacy subject. Thus rewrite runs filter-branch, moves the local branch, creates refs/original/, and only then refuses in post-verification. CRLF is valid commit-message data, so the rewrite is incomplete for an input its verifier explicitly recognizes.
issues.fix_hint: Split each line into content and its exact line terminator (supporting at least `\n`, `\r\n`, and `\r`), sanitize only the content, then append the terminator byte-for-byte. Add a non-vacuous test with a real CRLF legacy claim message that proves scan reports an exposure before rewrite, rewrite succeeds, the subject is handle-free afterward, and the remaining message bytes/line ending are preserved.
issues.title: CRLF legacy claim lines are detected but not sanitized

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The regate-sweep clock injection is correctly carried into Sweeper and the new entry-point controls distinguish a live dry run from an expired/inert sweep. However, the history purge has a message-boundary mismatch: scan recognizes legacy claim lines terminated with CRLF, while sanitize_message passes the trailing carriage return into sanitize_subject, whose anchored regex then does not match. Rewrite therefore changes the local ref and creates refs/original/, then fails its post-scan with the exposure still present. Because this prevents the documented purge from completing on valid Git commit-message bytes and consumes the one-shot backup namespace, I am requesting changes. This is a new major finding after round 4's clean verdict, so progress is regressing.
